text:
Adam Klapka is 6-foot-8, undrafted, and turning into a useful NHL forward. A Calgary Herald column on Nov. 5 called it Craig Conroy's patience paying off, with Klapka and Martin Pospisil both thriving, and six days later he scored on the power play against the Rangers. He has four goals and seven points in 20 games on 12 minutes a night, against 18 points in 79 games last season.

The finishing is real enough: he's at 12.9%, right around his expected rate, and his chances per 60 are up from 0.58 to 0.82. He has 72 hits, and he uses the size the way you'd hope, around the net. His ice time has climbed lately, near 15 minutes in four of his last five games.

The catch is the other end. Calgary takes only 44% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, four points worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season. He's a bottom-six forward with a 91 mph shot (94th percentile) who has found a role. Watch whether the Flames keep him on the power play, where the size does its best work.
